text:
alex: thinking about collapsing ingress backpressure and fallback into a single 'admission' stage to avoid per-request state scattered across proxy -> router -> runtime. Proposal: ingress decides accept/queue/fallback early based on cost model and available streaming slots. Thoughts? :thinking:

mira: hmm, do you mean move decision before auth/tokens? we'll need to ensure auth still can reject. also how to handle midstream capacity shifts?

alex: not before auth; after auth but before routing. auth still fully rejects. admission uses normalized tokens and a soft queue. If capacity drops midstream we send a small 503-with-retry-hint or try a fast fallback variant w/ compressed model.

sam: sounds neat but risks exposing more surface to gateway (memory + timers). what's budget per-tenant? eviction semantics?

alex: per-tenant budget + global soft limit. eviction by oldest prefix checkpoint. plan to keep only small per-stream metadata (owner, seq, kv-checkpoint-hash) — ideally <512 bytes per inflight stream.

priyanka: metrics question — we need per-path fallback rate and latency breakdown. Also traces must propagate fallback reason so product teams can correlate regressions.

mira: agree. don't forget SLOs: if we trigger fallback we should record `fallback_allowed=true` in trace attributes and in cost accounting.

devon: minor nit: streaming handoff must preserve client TCP/HTTP connection semantics. do not terminate client stream early unless we send final trailer explaining fallback. example trailer header: `x-redwood-fallback: model-downgrade;reason=capacity`

alex: exact. plan to send deterministic trailer and include a small summary JSON in the trailers: ```{
  "fallback": "lite-model-v2",
  "reason": "capacity_preempt",
  "tokens_served": 24
}```

sam: how do we reconcile with retries? if client retries we shouldn't double-charge. need idempotency token persistence across admission windows.

priyanka: agreed. suggest storing idempotency -> token mapping for TTL=30s and charge attribution at finalization. Also surface a metric: `fallback.retry_replay_conflicts` so we detect misbehaving clients.

mira: question about implementation: do we want this in the edge proxy or router service? decoupling is cleaner if we implement admission as a sidecar that owns the queue.

alex: sidecar makes deployments harder (more moving parts). prefer edge-proxy owning admission for single-hop decision and lower latency. we can factor into modules and toggle via feature flag for canary.

infra-bot: perf-test on branch alex/ingress-admission-refactor failed: latency regression +12% at 90p under synthetic video-transcription load. See CI: https://ci.redwood/jobs/9072

devon: can we adjust batch window heuristics? maybe allow short hedging and adaptive prefetch to reduce 90p while preserving cost.

alex: yes I'll iterate. next steps: prototype memory-bounded metadata store, add tracing flags, update rollout plan to canary 5% dedicated, request reviews @mira @priyanka @sam. PR: https://github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/832 :rocket:
